rater.kind: independent AI difficulty rater with explicit rubric, answer-free packet
rater.rubric: easy: one routine step or one familiar fact/formula applied directly; roughly 70%+ of test-takers correct; fits the first third of an ACT Math section. | medium: two or three routine steps, or a standard concept with a small twist; roughly 40-70% correct; middle third. | hard: needs a non-obvious insight or setup, combines two or more concepts, involves an unfamiliar application, or has a trap that catches most students who work quickly; roughly under 40% correct; last third. Length or arithmetic volume alone does NOT make an item hard.

CLD-ACT-M-000001.key_insight: Power of a power multiplies exponents, then add exponents
CLD-ACT-M-000001.tempting_wrong_path: Adding 3/2+4 to get x^(11/2)-type errors or forgetting the x^-1 (x^6)

CLD-ACT-M-000002.tempting_wrong_path: Rounding 9.58 up to 10 or ignoring the fee (12)
CLD-ACT-M-000002.why: Routine one-inequality setup with a floor.

CLD-ACT-M-000003.key_insight: Infinite solutions means the second equation is a scalar multiple (factor 1.5)
CLD-ACT-M-000003.tempting_wrong_path: Matching coefficients without the sign or using ratio 6/4 on wrong term (-4 or 9)
CLD-ACT-M-000003.why: Standard concept but students must recall the proportional-coefficients condition.

CLD-ACT-M-000005.key_insight: Sector area = (1/2)·r·arc length, or set up two equations in r and theta
CLD-ACT-M-000005.tempting_wrong_path: Treating 4pi as circumference or confusing arc and area formulas (2 or 2√6)
CLD-ACT-M-000005.why: Two linked sector formulas; small twist of solving for r.

CLD-ACT-M-000007.why: Classic successive-percent trap, but well known.

CLD-ACT-M-000008.key_insight: Target depth is 1.2-0.3=0.9 m so rise is 0.5 m; convert to liters
CLD-ACT-M-000008.tempting_wrong_path: Using rise of 0.8 m (to 0.3 below top misread) giving 67, or filling to top
CLD-ACT-M-000008.why: Multi-step volume/rate with a reading trap.

CLD-ACT-M-000009.why: Routine complex multiplication with a sign trap.

CLD-ACT-M-000010.why: Standard quadratic with factoring of leading coefficient 2.

CLD-ACT-M-000011.key_insight: Clearing denominators gives x=2, which is excluded
CLD-ACT-M-000011.why: Extraneous-solution trap catches most fast workers.

CLD-ACT-M-000012.key_insight: Slope 3 from table, intercept from f(1)
CLD-ACT-M-000012.why: Read slope and intercept from a table.

CLD-ACT-M-000013.key_insight: Solve 2^(t/5)=50 using logs or backsolve with calculator
CLD-ACT-M-000013.tempting_wrong_path: Forgetting to multiply by 5 (5.6) or dividing linearly (250)
CLD-ACT-M-000013.why: Exponential model; logs hard but backsolving choices makes it accessible.

CLD-ACT-M-000014.key_insight: Midpoint is center; radius is half the diameter length
CLD-ACT-M-000014.tempting_wrong_path: Using the diameter (100) or not squaring radius (5)

CLD-ACT-M-000015.key_insight: Area ratio 9/4 → length ratio 3/2 → volume ratio 27/8
CLD-ACT-M-000015.why: Similarity scaling across dimensions is a non-obvious, frequently missed insight.

CLD-ACT-M-000016.tempting_wrong_path: Computing only the complement 7/44 or a single-pick probability 5/12
CLD-ACT-M-000016.why: Combinations plus complement reasoning, two concepts.

CLD-ACT-M-000017.key_insight: Median is the 8th value in the cumulative frequency
CLD-ACT-M-000017.tempting_wrong_path: Taking median of the frequency row or the book values themselves (3) or mean (1.8)
CLD-ACT-M-000017.why: Frequency table median with a mild trap.

CLD-ACT-M-000018.key_insight: Add rates (0.4+0.3 pages/s), divide, convert seconds to minutes
CLD-ACT-M-000018.tempting_wrong_path: Unit conversion errors or averaging rates

CLD-ACT-M-000020.key_insight: Set up and solve a 2x2 linear system

CLD-ACT-M-000021.key_insight: g(1)=f(3)−5, so shift left 2 and down 5
CLD-ACT-M-000021.why: Horizontal-shift direction trap catches most students.

CLD-ACT-M-000022.key_insight: Symmetry puts vertex at x=2, so f=a(x−2)^2+9; solve a=−1
CLD-ACT-M-000022.tempting_wrong_path: Assuming a=1 or not using symmetry
CLD-ACT-M-000022.why: Requires vertex-from-symmetry insight plus vertex form.

CLD-ACT-M-000024.tempting_wrong_path: Using base·height with height 12 (72√3) or s^2/4

CLD-ACT-M-000025.key_insight: Conditional: denominator is all online students (114)
CLD-ACT-M-000025.why: Two-way table conditional probability with denominator trap.

CLD-ACT-M-000026.tempting_wrong_path: Price difference in dollars (96) or a single unit price (18, 20)

CLD-ACT-M-000028.tempting_wrong_path: Setting up concentrations without total volume
CLD-ACT-M-000028.why: Standard mixture setup many students find awkward.

CLD-ACT-M-000029.tempting_wrong_path: Sign error subtracting v (√61) or subtracting magnitudes
CLD-ACT-M-000029.why: Vector arithmetic plus magnitude; less-practiced topic.

CLD-ACT-M-000030.why: Routine linear equation, also easily backsolved.

CLD-ACT-M-000031.key_insight: Square, solve quadratic, then check for extraneous root
CLD-ACT-M-000031.why: Extraneous-root check is skipped by most quick solvers.

CLD-ACT-M-000033.why: One formula, but trig is less familiar to many.

CLD-ACT-M-000034.key_insight: Slope 3/4 → perpendicular −4/3, then point-slope to intercept
CLD-ACT-M-000034.why: Several routine steps with sign traps.

CLD-ACT-M-000035.why: Inscribed-square relation is a small twist.

CLD-ACT-M-000036.key_insight: Fill restricted first and last positions (5·5), then middle 8·7
CLD-ACT-M-000036.why: Constrained counting principle with ordering insight.

CLD-ACT-M-000041.tempting_wrong_path: Not distributing or wrong base conversion

CLD-ACT-M-000042.tempting_wrong_path: Computing derivative-like value or difference without dividing (12)

CLD-ACT-M-000043.key_insight: 18/b = 2·3^2/b so log = p+2q−1 via product, power, and log_b b=1
CLD-ACT-M-000043.tempting_wrong_path: Treating log_b 9 as q^2 or subtracting b
CLD-ACT-M-000043.why: Multiple log properties; logs are weak for most students.

CLD-ACT-M-000044.key_insight: Cylinder plus half of the sphere volume
CLD-ACT-M-000044.why: Composite solid with a half-volume trap.

CLD-ACT-M-000045.key_insight: Similar triangles ratio 6:10 → area ratio 9:25, ABC=150, subtract
CLD-ACT-M-000045.tempting_wrong_path: Using 6:4 ratio or linear scaling, or answering ABC (150)
CLD-ACT-M-000045.why: Similarity area-ratio plus subtraction with multiple traps.

CLD-ACT-M-000047.key_insight: Most spread from mean = largest SD

CLD-ACT-M-000048.tempting_wrong_path: Using a single average mpg or 420/30
